newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Aramco, Portugal's Petrogal in stake accord -paper.
newsitem.headline: Aramco, Portugal's Petrogal in stake accord -paper.

text.p: Saudi Aramco, the Saudi Arabian state oil company, has agreed in principle to buy a 27.5 percent stake in Portugal's state-controlled Petrogal energy company, the Diario Economico newspaper reported on Thursday.

The amount of the holding, the subject of long-running negotiations, was finally set at recent talks, it said. The accord must still be formally approved by the governments of both countries, it added.
No official comment was immediately available.
The accord, which the newspaper said included a long-term oil supply contract of between five and 10 years, would see the Portuguese state's holding dropping below 50 percent.
At present, the state has 55 percent of Petrogal, with the remaining shares being held by a Portuguese consortium, Petrocontrol.
Under the accord, which is expected to be finalised before the end of the year, Petrocontrol's stake will drop to 27.5 percent, the same as Saudi Aramco, the paper said.
In the past, the government has said that it would also be floating a part of Petrogal on the bourse.
The newspaper gave no financial details although it said the entry of Saudi Aramco would not involve any capital increase.
The Saudis and Portugal have been discussing the possibility of Aramco, the world's largest state-owned oil company, taking a stake in Petrogal for over a year.
